name: Nordvik Flex-Shaft Hoof Boot
description: A structured ankle boot designed specifically for partial-hoof geneware — the forefoot is a rigid polymer shell shaped to a hoof profile, while the rear section is padded leather with a flexible shaft. It bridges the gap between the hoof and the ankle cleanly, with a small heel block for balance. Comes in matte black and a dark mahogany. It's a niche product that does exactly one thing well: making partial-hoof geneware wearable in urban environments without wrapping the hoof in improvised foam. Tier 2-3 range.
functionality: Rigid hoof-profile forefoot shell protects and supports partial hoof geneware. Flexible rear shaft for ankle mobility.
what_it_says: You went hoof and you're not embarrassed — you just want to walk on pavement without cracking the geneware.
worn_by: people who got unusual mods for personal reasons
story_hooks: Nordvik's hoof shell molds are black-market copied constantly — the fakes use brittle resin that shatters under impact.
A Nordvik employee has been quietly modifying the hoof shells for paying customers to include hidden compartments.
